info.title: Hoardwise API
info.description:
The Hoardwise budget API. Every route is under `/api` and speaks JSON.

## Amounts, dates and months

- Amounts are integers in the smallest currency unit (pence or cents), never decimals. A transaction, target,
  pot or recurring amount is positive and at most 1,000,000,000. Account balances are sent as `pence`.
- Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`, months are `YYYY-MM` and timestamps are ISO 8601.

## Glossary

- Transaction `type`: `EXPENSE` is Spend, `INCOME` is Income, `SET_ASIDE` is Add to pot and `TAKE_OUT` is
  Take from pot.
- A budget is a category target (`/api/targets`), weekly or monthly.
- A pot is a category whose balance carries over from month to month.

## Examples and the clock

Pot and recurring examples assume the server clock is in October 2026 (UTC). `listPots`, `putPot` and
`archivePot` reject a month more than one month away from the server's current UTC month, so the `2026-10`
values in those examples fail outside September to November 2026.

The `addAccountBalance` example records a balance on 2026-10-29; the date may be at most one day after the
server's current UTC date, so it fails if the clock is before 28 October 2026.

## Authentication

There are two ways to authenticate, and every operation accepts either unless its `x-token-access` says otherwise.

- A browser session: the Auth0 JWT as a Bearer token (Auth0 mode), or the session cookie set by the built-in
  login (local mode). Cookie-authenticated requests that change data must send an `Origin` header matching the
  app's origin (`APP_ORIGIN` when set, otherwise the host).
- A personal API token, created on the Access tokens page or with `POST /api/tokens`, sent as
  `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A read token starts `hwr_` and a read-write token starts `hww_`. Examples in this
  document use placeholders such as `hwr_EXAMPLE`; never paste a real token into shared text.

Token rules:

- A read token may only make `GET` and `HEAD` requests. Any other method returns 403
  `This token is read-only`. A read-write token may use every method.
- A token can never reach `/api/tokens*`, `/api/push*` or `/api/auth/*`; those return 403
  `Not available to access tokens`. Each operation records this as `x-token-access`: `none` (no token),
  `read` (a read token is enough) or `write` (a read-write token is needed).
- A token is shown once when it is created, expires when its owner chose, can be revoked, and in local mode
  is revoked for good by a password reset (AUTH-15; Auth0 mode has no local password reset).
- Repeated failed token lookups from one client address are rate limited and answered with 429 and a
  `Retry-After` header. The limit is exact in the self-hosted container and best-effort per instance on AWS.

`/api/auth/*` (login, logout, setup and recovery for the built-in login) is not described here.

## Errors

An error response has a JSON body `{ "error": "<message>" }`, and some add extra fields. The statuses are 400
(invalid input), 401 (missing or invalid credential), 403 (forbidden, including token limits and protected
default categories), 404 (unknown route or record), 409 (conflict with the current state), 429 (too many
requests; see `Retry-After`) and 500 (an unexpected server failure, with a generic message).

## HEAD

`HEAD` on any `GET` operation returns the same status and headers as `GET` with no body. `HEAD` operations are not
listed separately. A path with no `GET` operation (for example `/api/categories/{categoryId}/reassign`) and an
unknown path answer `HEAD` with 404, as they do `GET`.

servers.description: The same origin that serves the app.

tags.name: categories
tags.description: Spending and income categories, including pot categories.

tags.name: targets
tags.description: Budgets (category targets), weekly or monthly, one per category.

tags.name: recurring
tags.description: Reminders for bills and income that repeat.

tags.name: accounts
tags.description: Savings, investments and debts, with a balance history.

tags.name: trash
tags.description: Deleted items that can be restored.

tags.name: push
tags.description: Web push reminder subscriptions. Not available to access tokens.

tags.name: tokens
tags.description: Personal API token management. Not available to access tokens.

tags.name: docs
tags.description: This API's own documentation, for scripts and agents. A read token can fetch it.

get.description: Returns the 21 built-in default categories followed by the household's custom categories (in id order). A pot category that has been archived carries `archived: true`; other categories omit the field.

post.description: Creates a category with a server-generated UUID id. When `group` is omitted it defaults to `SINKING_FUNDS` for a `POT`, nothing for `INCOME` and `EVERYDAY` for an `EXPENSE`. `name` is trimmed before it is stored.

pot.summary: A pot with the default group

put.description: Only the name can change. Default categories (ids starting `cat-` that ship with the app) cannot be renamed. The `categoryId` must be a custom category, for example the id returned by `createCategory`.

403.description: A default category cannot be renamed (`Cannot rename a default category`), or the credential may not make this request (see the shared `Forbidden` response).

404.description: No custom category has this id (`Category not found`).

delete.description: A hard delete: the category is removed for good and nothing goes to the trash. Transactions and reminders that use it are not changed; use `reassignCategory` first to move them. Deleting is idempotent by design: an id that does not exist is a deliberate 204. Default categories cannot be deleted.

204.description: The category is gone. No body.

403.description: A default category cannot be deleted (`Cannot delete a default category`), or the credential may not make this request (see the shared `Forbidden` response).

post.summary: Move a category's transactions and reminders to another category
post.description: Re-points every transaction and recurring reminder that uses `categoryId` at `toCategoryId`. The source id is not checked, so an id with no records returns zero counts. The destination must be a default category or an existing custom category.

put.description: Creates or replaces the target for the category. The category must exist, as a built-in default or one of the household's custom categories. The category is looked up first, so an unknown id is a 404 even when the body is invalid.

404.description: No category has this id (`Category not found`).

delete.description: Moves the target to the trash, where it can be restored. Deleting is idempotent by design: removing a target that does not exist is a deliberate 204, and adds nothing to the trash.

204.description: The target is removed. No body.

get.description: Returns every transaction stored under the given month. `month` is zero-padded, so `3` and `03` both mean March. Both values are checked strictly: `year` is exactly four digits and at least 2000, and `month` is one or two digits from 1 to 12. Anything else (such as `2026x`, `1x` or `1.5`) is a 400. A transaction belongs to the month in its `yearMonth` field, which is the first 7 characters of its `date`.

200.description: The month's transactions (an empty list when there are none).

400.description: `year` or `month` is missing (`year and month query parameters are required`) or not a four-digit year of 2000 or later and a month from 1 to 12 (`Invalid year or month`).

example.error: year and month query parameters are required

post.description: Stores a transaction in the month given by the first 7 characters of `date`. The server sets `yearMonth` and `createdAt`. The id is a server-generated UUID unless the client supplies `transactionId`, which lets a client retry safely. This is a deliberate idempotent create: supplying an id that already exists in that month replaces that transaction and still returns 201, because the offline queue replays a create with the entry's own id and must not fail or duplicate it. `categoryId` and `recurringId` are deliberately not checked against existing records, so a transaction may refer to a category or reminder that does not exist (or was deleted). `date` must be a real calendar date, so `2026-13-45` and `2026-02-30` are a 400 (`date must be a real date in YYYY-MM-DD format`). `recurringId` may be null, which means no link. `description` may be omitted or null and is stored as an empty string. Unknown fields are ignored.

income.summary: Salary, with the id left to the server

get.description: Returns the transactions whose `yearMonth` falls from `from` to `to` inclusive. The range is at most 24 months. Months are compared as `YYYY-MM` strings.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The last month, as `YYYY-MM`. Must not be before `from`, and at most 24 months from it inclusive.

200.description: The transactions in the range (an empty list when there are none).

400.description: `from` or `to` is missing or not a month (`from and to must be months in YYYY-MM format`), `from` is after `to` (`from must not be after to`), or the range is over 24 months (`the range must be at most 24 months`).

example.error: from must not be after to

put.description: Replaces every field of an existing transaction; the body is the same as for `createTransaction` (a `transactionId` in the body is ignored, the path id is kept). The path `yearMonth` is where the transaction is found. If the new `date` is in a different month, the transaction is moved there in one step: it keeps its id and `createdAt`, and the response carries the new `yearMonth`, so the old `yearMonth/transactionId` path stops working. `recurringId` keeps its stored link when omitted, replaces it when a UUID, and removes it when `null` (the response then has no `recurringId`). The path month must be a real `YYYY-MM` (`2026-13` is a 400). `date` must be a real calendar date, as for `createTransaction`; only writes are validated, so a stored transaction with an odd date still appears in lists.

404.description: No transaction with this id exists in the path month (`Transaction not found`).

delete.description: Moves the transaction to the trash, where `restoreFromTrash` can bring it back for 30 days. In the trash its `entityType` is `TRANSACTION` and its `id` is `<yearMonth>#<transactionId>`. Deleting a transaction that does not exist still returns 204 and adds nothing to the trash. The path month must be a real `YYYY-MM` (`2026-13` is a 400).

204.description: The transaction is deleted. No body.

400.description: The path `yearMonth` is not in `YYYY-MM` format (`yearMonth must be in YYYY-MM format`).

example.error: yearMonth must be in YYYY-MM format

get.description: Returns one `PotSummary` per pot category: the built-in pots (Holidays, Home maintenance, Gifts, Insurance, Emergency fund, Investment) followed by the household's custom pot categories. Archived pots are included and carry a non-null `archivedAt`. A pot's balance carries over from month to month and is worked out from its transactions (`SET_ASIDE` adds, `TAKE_OUT` and `EXPENSE` subtract; `INCOME` is ignored) and its automatic contributions, from the earliest month with any activity up to `asOf`. A pot with no activity has an empty `months` list, a zero balance and a zero `thisMonth`. Transactions dated after `asOf` are ignored.

parameters.name: asOf
parameters.description: The month to work out balances for, as `YYYY-MM`. It may be in the past, and at most one month after the server's current month (UTC). The example assumes the server clock is in October 2026 (UTC).

200.description: The pots (abridged in this example; the real list has one entry for every pot category).

400.description: `asOf` is missing, not a `YYYY-MM` month, or more than one month ahead (`asOf must be a month in YYYY-MM format, at most one month ahead`).

example.error: asOf must be a month in YYYY-MM format, at most one month ahead

put.summary: Set a pot's monthly amount, goal and automatic contribution
put.description: Creates or replaces the pot's settings. All four body fields are required. `monthlyAmount` and `goalAmount` are positive integer pence, or `null` for none (omitting them is a 400, not the same as null). `autoContribute: true` adds `monthlyAmount` to the pot automatically every month from `month`; it needs a non-null `monthlyAmount`. The setting is stored as a history (`autoContribute` in the response): saving removes every entry that starts in `month` or later, then adds `{from: month, amount}` only if the amount in force before `month` is different (the amount is `monthlyAmount` when on, `0` when off). The history may hold at most 120 entries. `month` is the first month the change applies to and must be within one month of the server's current month (UTC). An archived pot cannot be changed: call `unarchivePot` first (409). `categoryId` must be a built-in or custom category of type `POT`. Unknown body fields are ignored.

autoOn.summary: Save 50.00 a month towards a 1,200.00 goal

400.description: The body is not a JSON object (`Invalid JSON body`); `monthlyAmount` or `goalAmount` is missing or not null or a positive integer of at most 1,000,000,000 (`monthlyAmount must be null or a positive integer of pence`, and the same for `goalAmount`); `autoContribute` is not a boolean (`autoContribute must be a boolean`); `month` is missing, malformed or not within one month of now (`month must be a YYYY-MM month within one month of now`); `autoContribute` is true with a null `monthlyAmount` (`autoContribute needs a monthlyAmount`); `categoryId` is not a pot category (`categoryId must be an existing pot category`); or the history would exceed 120 entries (`Too many auto-contribute changes for this pot`).

409.description: The pot is archived (`Unarchive this pot before changing it`). Nothing was changed.

example.error: Unarchive this pot before changing it

post.description: Retires a pot that is empty. The pot's balance as at `month`, counting only real transactions and the automatic contributions made before `month`, must be exactly zero, otherwise the call is a 409 with the balance. On success the pot is marked archived (`archivedAt`, kept if it was already archived), automatic contributions stop from `month` (history entries that start in `month` or later are removed, so `month` itself gets no automatic contribution, which is deliberate because the pot is being closed and the balance must already be settled; if a non-zero contribution was in force before `month`, `{from: month, amount: 0}` is appended, otherwise `autoContribute` can end up empty), the monthly amount and goal are kept, and every recurring reminder in this category is moved to the trash (`cancelledRecurring` counts them; `restoreFromTrash` can bring them back for 30 days). The body must be exactly `{ "month": "YYYY-MM" }` with `month` within one month of the server's current month (UTC). The balance check comes first, so a pot with a balance trashes nothing. The reminders are then trashed one by one before the archived settings are saved: if that fails part-way (a 500) the pot is still active, and calling archive again trashes the reminders that are left and archives the pot. Reminders already trashed are not listed again, so `cancelledRecurring` on the retry counts only those the retry trashed.

cancelledRecurring.description: How many recurring reminders in this category were moved to the trash.

400.description: The body is not a JSON object of exactly `{ month }`, or `month` is malformed or not within one month of now (`Body must be { month } as a YYYY-MM month within one month of now`); or `categoryId` is not a pot category (`categoryId must be an existing pot category`).

example.error: Body must be { month } as a YYYY-MM month within one month of now

409.description: The pot still holds money (or is overdrawn). Nothing was changed.

balance.description: The non-zero balance in pence as at `month`; negative when overdrawn.

example.error: Take the balance out of this pot before archiving it

post.description: Clears `archivedAt`. The request needs no body, and any body is ignored. Nothing else is restored: the automatic contribution stays stopped (turn it on again with `putPot`) and reminders trashed by archiving stay in the trash until they are restored with `restoreFromTrash`. A pot that is not archived, including one with no stored settings, is a 409 and nothing is created or changed.

400.description: `categoryId` is not a pot category (`categoryId must be an existing pot category`).

example.error: categoryId must be an existing pot category

409.description: The pot is not archived (`This pot is not archived`). Nothing was changed.

get.description: Returns every recurring reminder, mapped (no storage keys), in id order. A reminder stored before `frequency` existed reads as `MONTHLY`.

post.description: Creates a reminder with a server-generated UUID id and `handledPeriod: null`. A monthly reminder (`frequency` `MONTHLY`, which is also the default when `frequency` is omitted or null) needs `dayOfMonth` and ignores `anchorDate`. Every other frequency needs a real `anchorDate`, ignores any `dayOfMonth` in the body and stores `dayOfMonth` as the day of the anchor date. `leadDays` (how many days before the due date the reminder starts) defaults to 3 and may be at most 14 for `WEEKLY` and `FOUR_WEEKLY`, 30 for `MONTHLY` and 60 for `QUARTERLY` and `YEARLY`. `description` is trimmed after its 200-character limit is checked. The `categoryId` is not checked against existing categories. Unknown fields are ignored.

weekly.summary: A weekly payment counted from a date

400.description: The body is not a JSON object (`Invalid JSON body`) or a field breaks a rule. The messages are `amount must be a positive integer representing pence/cents, at most 1000000000`, `type must be EXPENSE, INCOME, SET_ASIDE, or TAKE_OUT`, `categoryId is required` (missing, empty or over 100 characters), `description must be a string of at most 200 characters`, `frequency must be one of WEEKLY, FOUR_WEEKLY, MONTHLY, QUARTERLY, YEARLY`, `leadDays must be an integer from 0 to <max> for <FREQUENCY> items`, `dayOfMonth must be an integer from 1 to 31` (monthly) and `anchorDate must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date for <FREQUENCY> items` (other frequencies; `2026-02-30` is not valid). The first rule broken, in that order, is reported.

example.error: dayOfMonth must be an integer from 1 to 31

put.description: Replaces the editable fields of an existing reminder; the body and its rules are the same as for `createRecurring`. This is deliberately a full replacement, not a patch: an omitted `frequency` means `MONTHLY` (so a weekly reminder sent without `frequency` becomes monthly), an omitted `description` becomes empty and an omitted `leadDays` goes back to 3. `recurringId` and `createdAt` are kept. `handledPeriod` is kept when the frequency is unchanged and cleared to `null` when it changes, because its format depends on the frequency; a reminder stored without a `frequency` counts as `MONTHLY`. The id is looked up first, so an unknown id is a 404 whatever the body holds.

400.description: The reminder exists but the body is not a JSON object (`Invalid JSON body`) or breaks a rule listed under `createRecurring`.

404.description: No reminder has this id (`Recurring item not found`). The id is checked before the body, so an invalid body for an unknown id is still a 404.

delete.description: Moves the reminder to the trash, where `restoreFromTrash` can bring it back for 30 days (`entityType` `RECURRING`, `id` the reminder's id). Deleting a reminder that does not exist still returns 204 and adds nothing to the trash. Transactions made from the reminder keep their `recurringId`.

204.description: The reminder is deleted. No body.

post.summary: Mark a reminder handled, or clear the mark
post.description: Records the latest occurrence that has been dealt with, so the reminder stops showing for it. `period` is `YYYY-MM` for a monthly reminder and the occurrence date `YYYY-MM-DD` (a real calendar date) for the other frequencies, or `null` to clear the mark. The format must match the reminder's frequency: a monthly reminder rejects a date and every other frequency rejects a bare month (400 naming the expected format). The reminder is looked up first, so an unknown id is a 404 whatever the body holds. The field is required (an empty object is a 400). Only `handledPeriod` and `updatedAt` change.

month.summary: A monthly reminder handled for October

occurrence.summary: A weekly reminder handled for one date

400.description: The reminder exists but the body is not a JSON object (`Invalid JSON body`), `period` is missing or is neither a string nor null (`period must be YYYY-MM, YYYY-MM-DD or null`), or the string is the wrong format for the reminder's frequency (`period must be a YYYY-MM month for a monthly item`, or `period must be a real YYYY-MM-DD date for a weekly, four-weekly, quarterly or yearly item`).

example.error: period must be a YYYY-MM month for a monthly item

404.description: No reminder has this id (`Recurring item not found`). The id is checked before the body, so an invalid body for an unknown id is still a 404.

get.description: Returns the deleted transactions, budgets (targets), recurring reminders and accounts that can still be restored, newest deletion first. An item stays for 30 days after deletion; expired items are not listed and cannot be restored. Items are added by deleting a transaction, budget, reminder or account, and by archiving a pot, which trashes that category's recurring reminders. Deleted categories are not kept.

post.description: Puts a trashed item back exactly as it was stored and removes it from the trash. Only `entityType` and `id` are accepted; any other field is a 400. The item is restored under its original key, so it is not restored if something now occupies that key.

item.description: The restored record, without storage keys. Same shape as `item` in `listTrash`.

400.description: The body is not a JSON object (`Invalid JSON body`), has a field other than `entityType` and `id` (`Only entityType and id are allowed`), has a missing or unknown `entityType` (`entityType must be one of TRANSACTION, TARGET, RECURRING, ACCOUNT`), or has a missing or malformed `id` (`id is missing or not in the expected format`).

example.error: Only entityType and id are allowed

404.description: Nothing with this type and id is in the trash, or it has expired or was just restored by another request (`This item is no longer in Recently deleted`).

example.error: This item is no longer in Recently deleted

409.description: A record already exists at the original key, so nothing was restored and the item stays in the trash (`This item is already in place, so it was not restored`).

example.error: This item is already in place, so it was not restored

get.description: Returns every account with its full balance history (oldest date first), mapped (no storage keys), in id order. An account stored without a balance list reads with `balances: []`.

post.description: Creates an account with a server-generated UUID id and an empty balance history. `kind` says whether the account is money held (`ASSET`) or money owed (`LIABILITY`), and `type` must belong to that kind: `CASH`, `SAVINGS` or `INVESTMENT` for an `ASSET`; `CREDIT_CARD` or `LOAN` for a `LIABILITY`. `name` is trimmed before it is stored. Add balances with `addAccountBalance`.

400.description: The body is not a JSON object (`Invalid JSON body`); `name` is missing, blank or over 50 characters (`name must be a non-empty string of at most 50 characters`); `kind` is not `ASSET` or `LIABILITY` (`kind must be ASSET or LIABILITY`); or `type` does not belong to `kind` (`type must match kind: CASH, SAVINGS, INVESTMENT` for an asset, `type must match kind: CREDIT_CARD, LOAN` for a liability). The first rule broken, in that order, is reported.

example.error: type must match kind: CREDIT_CARD, LOAN

put.summary: Rename an account or change its type
put.description: Changes `name` and `type`; both are required. `kind` and the balance history cannot be changed here, and a `kind` in the body is ignored. The new `type` must belong to the account's existing `kind` (see `createAccount`). The account is looked up first, so an unknown id is a 404 even when the body is invalid.

400.description: The body is not a JSON object (`Invalid JSON body`); `name` is missing, blank or over 50 characters (`name must be a non-empty string of at most 50 characters`); or `type` does not belong to the account's kind (`type must match the account's existing kind: CASH, SAVINGS, INVESTMENT` for an asset, `... CREDIT_CARD, LOAN` for a liability).

example.error: name must be a non-empty string of at most 50 characters

404.description: No account has this id (`Account not found`).

delete.description: Moves the account, with its balance history, to the trash, where `restoreFromTrash` can bring it back for 30 days (`entityType` `ACCOUNT`, `id` the account id). Deleting an account that does not exist still returns 204 and adds nothing to the trash.

204.description: The account is deleted. No body.

post.description: Records the balance on a date. A balance is an integer `pence` that may be zero (an account paid off or closed) or negative (an overdrawn account), with a magnitude of at most 1,000,000,000. Recording a date that already has an entry replaces that entry; otherwise the entry is added. The history is kept sorted by date and holds at most 500 entries. `date` must be a real calendar date and no later than tomorrow (UTC), so the example assumes the server clock is no earlier than 28 October 2026 (UTC). The account is looked up first (an unknown account is a 404 even when the body is invalid), then the body is validated (400). Unknown body fields are ignored.

200.description: The account with the balance recorded.

400.description: The body is not a JSON object (`Invalid JSON body`); `date` is not a real `YYYY-MM-DD` date or is more than one day ahead (`date must be a YYYY-MM-DD date, at most one day ahead of today`); `pence` is not a whole number between -1,000,000,000 and 1,000,000,000 (`pence must be a whole number between -1000000000 and 1000000000`); or the account already has 500 entries on other dates (`an account can have at most 500 balance entries`).

example.error: pence must be a whole number between -1000000000 and 1000000000

404.description: No account has this id (`Account not found`).

post.summary: Turn on bill reminders for a device
post.description: Stores a browser push subscription and when it wants reminders, and signs the household up for the reminder scheduler. Not available to access tokens: a request with an access token is refused with 403 `Not available to access tokens`. The subscription is the object a browser's `PushManager.subscribe()` returns. A device is identified by its `endpoint`, so sending the same endpoint again replaces that device's settings and keys rather than adding a second one. At most 5 devices can have reminders on; a sixth distinct endpoint is a 409. The body may hold only `subscription` and `settings`, and `subscription` only `endpoint`, `keys` and `expirationTime` (any value; it is not stored).

200.description: The device is subscribed (created or updated).

400.description: The body is not a JSON object (`Invalid JSON body`) or breaks a rule. The messages are `Unexpected fields in the request`, `subscription is required`, `subscription.endpoint must be an https address of a supported push service, at most 1000 characters`, `subscription.keys must hold p256dh and auth as base64url text`, `settings are required`, `settings.hour must be a whole number from 0 to 23`, `quiet hours must be whole numbers from 0 to 23, or null`, `quietStart and quietEnd must both be set or both be null` and `settings.timeZone must be a valid time zone name`. The first rule broken, in that order, is reported.

example.error: settings.hour must be a whole number from 0 to 23

403.description: An access token was used (`Not available to access tokens`), or a cookie-authenticated request came from another origin.

409.description: Five other devices already have reminders on (`At most 5 devices can have reminders turned on`). Nothing was changed.

example.error: At most 5 devices can have reminders turned on

delete.summary: Turn off bill reminders for a device
delete.description: Removes the subscription for the given endpoint. Not available to access tokens: a request with an access token is refused with 403 `Not available to access tokens`. The body must be exactly `{ "endpoint": "<url>" }`, and the endpoint must pass the same allow-list as `createPushSubscription`. Removing an endpoint that is not subscribed still returns 204. When the household has no device left it drops out of the reminder scheduler.

204.description: The device has no reminders. No body.

400.description: The body is not a JSON object, or holds a field other than `endpoint` (`Invalid JSON body`); or `endpoint` is not an https address of a supported push service (`endpoint must be an https address of a supported push service`).

example.error: endpoint must be an https address of a supported push service

403.description: An access token was used (`Not available to access tokens`), or a cookie-authenticated request came from another origin.

get.description: Lists the household's personal API tokens, newest first. Not available to access tokens: a request with an access token is refused with 403 `Not available to access tokens`. A listing never includes the secret or its hash; `prefix` is only the first 8 characters, enough to recognise a token. The response carries `Cache-Control: no-store`. Expired tokens remain listed until they are purged.

403.description: An access token was used (`Not available to access tokens`), or the request was refused for another reason (see the shared `Forbidden` response).

post.description: Creates a personal API token. Not available to access tokens: a request with an access token is refused with 403 `Not available to access tokens`. The secret (`token`) is in the 201 response only; it is stored as a hash and cannot be shown again, so keep it somewhere safe. The response carries `Cache-Control: no-store`. A read token (`hwr_`) can only make `GET` (and `HEAD`) requests; a read-write token (`hww_`) can use every method. `expiryDays` is required: send 90, 180, 365 or 730, or `null` for a token that never expires. A household can have at most 25 tokens (409); revoke one first. In local mode (the built-in login), creating a `write` token also needs the account `password`: a missing password is a 403 `Password required`, a wrong one a 403 `Incorrect password`, and repeated wrong guesses (shared with the login screen) are throttled with a 429. `password` is ignored for a `read` token and in Auth0 mode. The password is checked before the 25-token cap, so a missing or wrong password is refused with 403/429 even when the cap is reached. It is never stored or logged. Unknown body fields are rejected.

read.summary: A read token that expires in 90 days

write.summary: A read-write token that never expires, in local mode

201.description: The token was created. This is the only time the secret is shown.

400.description: The body is not a JSON object (`Invalid JSON`) or breaks a rule. The messages are `Unexpected fields in the request`, `name is required` (missing, not a string or blank), `name must be at most 60 characters` (after trimming), `name must not contain control characters`, `scope must be 'read' or 'write'`, `expiryDays must be 90, 180, 365, 730 or null` (also when omitted) and `password must be a string of at most 128 characters`. The first rule broken, in that order, is reported.

403.description: An access token was used (`Not available to access tokens`); in local mode a `write` token was requested without the account password (`Password required`) or with the wrong one (`Incorrect password`); or the request was refused for another reason (see the shared `Forbidden` response).

missingPassword.summary: Local mode, write token, no password

wrongPassword.summary: Local mode, write token, wrong password

409.description: The household already has 25 tokens (`You can have at most 25 access tokens. Revoke one first.`).

example.error: You can have at most 25 access tokens. Revoke one first.

429.description: Too many requests (`Too many requests`, with `Retry-After`, as in the shared `TooManyRequests` response), or, in local mode when creating a `write` token, too many wrong passwords (`Too many attempts`). The password throttle adds `retryAfter` (seconds) to the body, sends `Retry-After`, and refuses even a correct password until it ends.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

delete.description: Revokes the token for good; requests that present it are refused from then on. Not available to access tokens: a request with an access token is refused with 403 `Not available to access tokens`. The response is 204 with no body and carries `Cache-Control: no-store`. An id that is not a UUID, does not exist or belongs to another household is a 404.

204.description: The token is revoked. No body.

403.description: An access token was used (`Not available to access tokens`), or the request was refused for another reason (see the shared `Forbidden` response).

404.description: No token of this household has this id (`Token not found`).

get.description: Returns this API's OpenAPI 3.1 document as JSON. It describes every route and holds no household data. A read token is enough.
Returns a compact Markdown reference to this API, grouped by topic, for an agent or a script. It holds no household data. A read token is enough.

bearerToken.description: An Auth0 JWT (Auth0 mode) or a personal API token starting `hwr_` (read) or `hww_` (read-write). Tokens are limited as described in the API overview.

sessionCookie.name: hoardwise_session
sessionCookie.description: The session cookie set by the built-in login (local mode). Over HTTPS it is named `__Host-hoardwise_session`.

yearMonth.name: yearMonth
yearMonth.description: The month a transaction belongs to, as `YYYY-MM`, with a month from 01 to 12.

potCategoryId.name: categoryId
potCategoryId.description: The id of a pot category, built-in (such as `cat-holidays`) or custom.

recurringId.name: recurringId
recurringId.description: The id of a recurring reminder.

tokenId.name: tokenId
tokenId.description: The id of an access token.

ValidationError.description: The request was invalid. The message says which field or rule.

Unauthorized.description: The credential is missing, invalid, expired or revoked.

Forbidden.description: The credential is valid but may not do this: a read token on a write method, a token on a route tokens cannot use, a cross-origin cookie request, or a protected default category.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with the current state.

example.error: This item is already in place, so it was not restored

TooManyRequests.description: Too many requests. Wait for the number of seconds in `Retry-After`.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

InternalError.description: An unexpected failure. The message is generic; the detail is in the server logs only.

Error.description: The body of every error response. Two errors add fields: the 409 from `archivePot` adds `balance`, and the 429 `Too many attempts` from `createAccessToken` (the password throttle) adds `retryAfter`. Other 429 responses (`Too many requests`) have no extra fields and signal the wait only in the `Retry-After` header.

error.description: A short message that is safe to show to the user.

categoryId.description: A fixed id such as `cat-groceries` for a default category, a UUID for a custom one.

icon.description: An emoji or an icon name. `default` when none was given.

isDefault.description: True for the built-in categories, which cannot be renamed or deleted.

createdAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp; the built-in categories share one fixed date.

archived.description: Present and true only for an archived pot category.

icon.description: An emoji or icon name, cut to 50 characters. A non-string is ignored and `default` is stored.

group.description: Not allowed for `INCOME`. A `POT` must use `SINKING_FUNDS` or `SAVING_INVESTMENT`; an `EXPENSE` must use `BILLS` or `EVERYDAY`.

toCategoryId.description: The category to move records to. It must exist and differ from the path `categoryId`.

TransactionType.description: What kind of movement this is. `EXPENSE` is Spend, `INCOME` is Income, `SET_ASIDE` is Add to pot and `TAKE_OUT` is Take from pot.

yearMonth.description: The month, `YYYY-MM`. Always equal to the first 7 characters of `date`.

description.description: Trimmed. An empty string when none was given.

recurringId.description: The recurring reminder this transaction was made from. Present only when linked.

transactionId.description: Create only, a client-chosen UUID. Ignored when updating.

description.description: Optional, at most 200 characters before trimming. Null or omitted is stored as an empty string.

date.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`, a real calendar date (`2026-02-30` is rejected).

recurringId.description: Links the transaction to a recurring reminder (a UUID); not checked against existing reminders. On create, null or omitted means no link. On update, omitted keeps the stored link, a UUID replaces it and null removes it.

PotAutoEntry.description: One step in a pot's automatic contribution history.

from.description: The first month the amount applies to, `YYYY-MM`. It applies until the next entry's month.

amount.description: Pence added to the pot each month. `0` means automatic contributions are off.

PotSettings.description: A pot's stored settings, without storage keys.

monthlyAmount.description: Pence the household plans to put in each month. Null means no plan.

goalAmount.description: Pence the pot is saving towards. Null means no goal.

autoContribute.description: The history of automatic contributions, oldest first. Empty when never turned on.

archivedAt.description: When the pot was archived. Null for an active pot.

monthlyAmount.description: Positive integer pence, or null for none. Required, but may be null.

goalAmount.description: Positive integer pence, or null for no goal. Required, but may be null.

autoContribute.description: Add `monthlyAmount` to the pot automatically every month from `month`. Needs a non-null `monthlyAmount`.

month.description: The first month the automatic contribution change applies to, `YYYY-MM`. Within one month either side of the server's current month (UTC). The example assumes the server clock is in October 2026 (UTC).
The month the pot is emptied by, `YYYY-MM`. Within one month either side of the server's current month (UTC). The example assumes the server clock is in October 2026 (UTC).

PotMonth.description: One month of a pot's history. All amounts are integer pence.

opening.description: The balance carried in from the previous month (0 for the first month).

setAside.description: Total of `SET_ASIDE` (Add to pot) transactions in the month.

autoAdded.description: The automatic contribution for the month.

takeOut.description: Total of `TAKE_OUT` (Take from pot) transactions in the month.

spent.description: Total of `EXPENSE` (Spend) transactions in the month.

closing.description: `opening + setAside + autoAdded - takeOut - spent`. Can be negative when overdrawn.

PotSummary.description: A pot with its settings and monthly history up to the requested month. All amounts are integer pence.

monthlyAmount.description: The planned monthly amount from the settings; null when never set or cleared.

goalAmount.description: The goal from the settings; null when never set or cleared.

autoAmountNow.description: The automatic contribution in force in the `asOf` month. 0 when off.

balance.description: The closing balance of the `asOf` month. 0 when the pot has no activity. Negative when overdrawn.

thisMonth.description: The movements in the `asOf` month (all zero when the pot has no activity).

months.description: Every month from the pot's first activity (a transaction, or the start of an automatic contribution) up to and including `asOf`, oldest first, with no gaps. Empty when the pot has no activity.

RecurringFrequency.description: How often the reminder repeats. `WEEKLY` every 7 days and `FOUR_WEEKLY` every 28 days, both counted from `anchorDate`; `MONTHLY` on `dayOfMonth`; `QUARTERLY` every three months and `YEARLY` every year, both counted from `anchorDate`.

Recurring.description: A reminder for a bill or income that repeats. Responses never include storage keys.

description.description: Trimmed. An empty string when none was given.

dayOfMonth.description: For `MONTHLY`, the day it falls due. For the other frequencies, the day of the month of `anchorDate`.

anchorDate.description: The date a non-monthly schedule is counted from, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Null for `MONTHLY`.

leadDays.description: How many days before the due date the reminder starts showing. At most 14 for `WEEKLY` and `FOUR_WEEKLY`, 30 for `MONTHLY` and 60 for `QUARTERLY` and `YEARLY`.

handledPeriod.description: The latest occurrence marked handled: `YYYY-MM` for a monthly reminder and the occurrence date `YYYY-MM-DD` for the others; null when none. `setRecurringHandled` enforces the format for the reminder's frequency, and `updateRecurring` resets it to null when the frequency changes.

RecurringInput.description: `dayOfMonth` is required when `frequency` is `MONTHLY` or omitted; `anchorDate` is required for every other frequency.

description.description: Optional, at most 200 characters before trimming. Null or omitted is stored as an empty string.

frequency.description: Defaults to `MONTHLY` when omitted or null.

dayOfMonth.description: Required for `MONTHLY`. Ignored for the other frequencies.

anchorDate.description: Required for the non-monthly frequencies, a real calendar date. Ignored for `MONTHLY`.

leadDays.description: Defaults to 3 when omitted or null. The maximum depends on `frequency` (see `Recurring`).

period.description: `YYYY-MM` (for monthly reminders), a real `YYYY-MM-DD` date (for the others) or null to clear. Required, but may be null.

TrashEntityType.description: What was deleted. `TRANSACTION` is a transaction, `TARGET` a budget, `RECURRING` a recurring reminder and `ACCOUNT` an account.

id.description: The id to send to `restoreFromTrash`. For `TRANSACTION` it is `<yearMonth>#<transactionId>`; for the other types it is the target's category id, the recurring id or the account id.

item.description: The deleted record as it was stored, without storage keys: a `Transaction`, a target, a recurring reminder or an account, according to `entityType`.

expiresAt.description: When the item stops being restorable, in Unix seconds (30 days after `deletedAt`).

id.description: The `id` from `listTrash`. For `TRANSACTION`, `YYYY-MM#<transactionId>`; otherwise 1 to 100 letters, digits, `_` or `-`. The transaction id part has the same character rules.

AccountKind.description: `ASSET` is money held; `LIABILITY` is money owed.

AccountType.description: `CASH`, `SAVINGS` and `INVESTMENT` belong to the `ASSET` kind; `CREDIT_CARD` and `LOAN` belong to the `LIABILITY` kind.

pence.description: Integer pence (or cents). Zero and negative balances are allowed. A liability is recorded as the amount owed.

Account.description: An account with its balance history. Responses never include storage keys.

balances.description: One entry per date, oldest first.

name.description: 1 to 50 characters, not blank. The length is checked before trimming.
1 to 50 characters, not blank. The length is checked before trimming.

date.description: A real calendar date, `YYYY-MM-DD`, no later than tomorrow (UTC). There is no earliest date.

pence.description: Integer pence (or cents); zero and negative values are allowed.

endpoint.description: An https address, with no user name, password or port, on a supported push service: `fcm.googleapis.com`, `updates.push.services.mozilla.com`, `web.push.apple.com` or a host ending `.notify.windows.com`.

expirationTime.description: Accepted, as sent by browsers, but ignored.

p256dh.description: The browser's public key, base64url text.

auth.description: The browser's auth secret, base64url text.

hour.description: The hour of the day (in `timeZone`) to send reminders.

quietStart.description: The hour quiet time starts, or null for no quiet hours. Null if and only if `quietEnd` is null.

quietEnd.description: The hour quiet time ends, or null for no quiet hours. Null if and only if `quietStart` is null.

timeZone.description: An IANA time zone name the platform recognises, such as `Europe/London`.

endpoint.description: The endpoint to remove; it must pass the same allow-list as in `PushSubscriptionInput`.

AccessToken.description: A personal API token as listed. It never includes the secret or its hash. Times are Unix seconds.

tokenId.description: A UUID, used to revoke the token.

scope.description: `read` tokens start `hwr_` and may only make `GET` (and `HEAD`) requests; `write` tokens start `hww_`.

createdAt.description: When the token was created, in Unix seconds.

expiresAt.description: When the token stops working, in Unix seconds. Null for a token that never expires.

lastUsedAt.description: When the token was last used, in Unix seconds, updated at most hourly. Null until first use.

prefix.description: The first 8 characters of the secret, to recognise it by.

NewAccessToken.description: A newly created token. This is the only response that carries the secret.

token.description: The secret, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A real one is `hwr_` (read) or `hww_` (read-write) followed by 43 URL-safe characters. It is not stored and cannot be shown again.

name.description: A label, at most 60 characters after trimming. Not blank, no control characters.

expiryDays.description: Days until the token expires, or null for never. Required, but may be null.

password.description: The account password. Used only in local mode when `scope` is `write`, where it is required; ignored otherwise.
